key_insight: MedRLM frames patient care as a recursive, multimodal reasoning process that can repeatedly inspect, retrieve, verify, and synthesize information across records, images, sensor streams, and guidelines.
clinical_relevance: The approach is designed to support more auditable clinical decision-making, especially for long, complex cases and abnormal sensor findings that may need escalation or referral.
method: Uses specialized agents for text, EHR, imaging, sensors, guideline retrieval, uncertainty auditing, and referral planning
Builds a Clinical Evidence Graph Memory to link patient observations with external evidence and referral criteria
Triggers deeper reasoning recursively when sensor patterns or uncertainty suggest higher risk
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a planned evaluation on public and credentialed datasets spanning EHR, radiology, ECG, ICU time series, and referral-proxy outcomes.
watch_item: Performance and safety will depend on reliable data integration and robust clinician oversight, especially for low-confidence or high-risk cases.
paper_title: MedRLM: Recursive Multimodal Health Intelligence for Long-Context Clinical Reasoning, Sensor-Guided Screening, Evidence-Grounded Decision Support, and Community-to-Tertiary Referral Optimization
